security_audit.summary: All 38 static findings are false positives involving Markdown syntax, documented service links, ordinary API authentication, post identifiers, or readable Chinese prose. The CLI examples introduce a separate supply-chain risk by automatically executing an unpinned npm package. No evidence found of prompt injection or credential exfiltration in the supplied files; the external package implementation was not provided.

remediation.issue: The CLI examples execute socialdatax-skills@latest with automatic npm confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited package version, verify dependency integrity, and require explicit approval before downloading and executing third-party code with API credentials.

semantic_findings.description: The examples use 'npx -y socialdatax-skills@latest', automatically selecting and executing a mutable npm release. A compromised release could access the configured API credential.

content.user_title: Analyze X / Twitter Comments for Customer Insights
content.value_statement: X / Twitter comment threads can hide useful customer feedback across many replies. This skill organizes retrieved comments into themes, concerns, FAQs, and practical actions.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve top-level comments by X post URL or post ID through the documented SocialDataX CLI or configured MCP tools.
Retrieve replies using a post ID and a top-level comment ID.
Continue pagination with returned tokens and optional page or item limits.
Organize visible feedback into themes, pain points, purchase concerns, unmet needs, and FAQs.
Separate quoted comment evidence from interpretation and state the retrieved sample coverage.
Preserve partial results and resume with available continuation tokens after recoverable failures.
limitations: Requires a SocialDataX API key, network access, and sufficient service balance; CLI usage also requires Node.js and npm.
Results cover only returned comments and replies for selected posts, not all X / Twitter discussions.
The documented workflow is read-only and does not log in, post, like, or reply on the user account.
The external npm package implementation is not included; its runtime behavior and future releases are outside this file review.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Product Feedback
use_cases.description: Review comments on a product announcement to identify recurring needs, purchase barriers, and evidence-backed improvement questions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Support FAQs
use_cases.description: Group questions and concerns under a brand post into draft FAQ topics with supporting comment evidence.

use_cases.title: Review Audience Reactions
use_cases.description: Analyze discussion themes and reply threads to prepare a content retrospective and follow-up topic list.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize One Comment Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the first returned comment page for [post URL]. Summarize themes and state the sample coverage. Quote only retrieved text.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Purchase Concerns
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve up to [item limit] comments for [post ID]. Group purchase concerns and unmet needs. Separate comment evidence from interpretation.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Reply Thread
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve replies for [post ID] and [comment ID], limited to [page limit] pages. Identify unresolved questions and draft FAQs from visible evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evidence-Based Action List
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [post URLs] using at most [item limit] comments per post. Compare themes, cite visible evidence, and propose actions. Disclose partial results and coverage.

output_examples.input: Illustrative sample: two retrieved comments ask whether an annual subscription is required. Summarize the purchase concern.
output_examples.output: Theme: subscription flexibility. Evidence: both supplied comments ask about annual commitment. Suggested action: clarify available billing options. Coverage: two comments only.

output_examples.input: Illustrative sample: one returned reply asks about offline access. Draft an FAQ topic without inventing product details.
output_examples.output: FAQ topic: Is offline access supported? Evidence: one supplied reply asks this question. Answer status: product confirmation required. Coverage: one reply.

best_practices: Start with one page and set explicit page or item limits before expanding collection.
Keep quotations faithful to returned text and state whether replies or additional pages were included.
Approve and review external dependencies before execution, and keep API credentials out of prompts and reports.
anti_patterns: Treating one post or one comment page as representative of all X / Twitter users.
Inventing customer quotations, product answers, or unsupported frequency claims.
Restarting partial collections from the first page or repeatedly retrying insufficient-balance errors.

faq.question: What input does this skill accept?
faq.answer: Provide an X / Twitter post URL or post ID. Reply retrieval also requires a top-level comment ID.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure SOCIALDATAX_API_KEY for SocialDataX authentication. Requests also require network access and sufficient service balance.

faq.question: Does it post replies or change my account?
faq.answer: The documented workflow only retrieves data. It does not log in, post, like, comment, or modify account settings.

faq.question: Can it retrieve more than one comment page?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents pagination tokens, page limits, item limits, and an all-pages option. The all-pages option has no default collection cap.

faq.question: Does the report represent all discussions on X?
faq.answer: No. Conclusions cover only retrieved comments and replies under the selected posts. Partial samples and incomplete retrieval must be disclosed.

faq.question: What happens when collection fails partway through?
faq.answer: Keep returned items and errors. Resume only with a nonempty continuation token, preserving the original query and remaining collection limits.
